{"id": 202, "title": "MAUD deal points pack — Merger Agreement (Aurelian Summit / Silverline Data Systems) execution version — tender offer terms, Offer conditions and MAE definition excerpt", "doc_type": "merger_agreement_excerpt", "related_shape": "maud-deal-points", "body": "CONFORMED EXCERPT — AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER, dated as of July 20, 2026, by and among Aurelian Summit Group plc, a public limited company organized under the laws of England and Wales ("Parent"), Summit Argent Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Parent ("Purchaser"), and Silverline Data Systems, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"). Excerpt of Article I (the Offer), Article VI (Conditions to the Offer) and the definition of Company Material Adverse Effect, prepared for the deal-points file by Ellsworth & Crane LLP from the EXECUTION VERSION.

Section 1.1 The Offer. Provided that this Agreement shall not have been terminated in accordance with Article VIII, Purchaser shall commence (within the meaning of Rule 14d-2 under the Exchange Act), as promptly as practicable and in any event within ten (10) Business Days after the date hereof, a tender offer (the "Offer") to purchase all of the issued and outstanding shares of Company Common Stock at a price per share of $47.25, net to the seller in cash, without interest (the "Offer Price"). This is a two-step transaction: as soon as practicable following the Acceptance Time, the Merger shall be effected without a vote of the Company's stockholders pursuant to Section 251(h) of the DGCL, and each share not accepted in the Offer (other than Excluded Shares and Dissenting Shares) shall be converted into the right to receive the Offer Price.

Section 6.1 Conditions to the Offer. Notwithstanding any other provision of the Offer, Purchaser shall not be required to accept for payment any shares of Company Common Stock validly tendered unless, at the scheduled Expiration Time: (a) the number of shares validly tendered and not validly withdrawn, together with shares owned by Parent and its Subsidiaries, represents at least a majority of the shares of Company Common Stock then outstanding (the "Minimum Condition"); (b) the waiting period under the HSR Act shall have expired or been terminated and the requisite foreign direct investment clearances obtained (the "Regulatory Condition"); (c) since the date of this Agreement there shall not have occurred a Company Material Adverse Effect that is continuing; and (d) the aggregate number of shares of Company Common Stock with respect to which the holders thereof have properly exercised and not withdrawn or lost appraisal rights under Section 262 of the DGCL (the "Dissenting Shares") shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the shares of Company Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the Expiration Time (the "Appraisal Rights Condition").

Section 8.1(b) Outside Date. Either Parent or the Company may terminate this Agreement if the Acceptance Time shall not have occurred on or before November 14, 2026 (the "Outside Date"), automatically extended to February 14, 2027 if on such date the Regulatory Condition (but no other condition) remains unsatisfied.

Definition — "Company Material Adverse Effect" (condensed). The definition follows the customary two-part structure, with carveouts for: general economic and financial market conditions; conditions generally affecting the Company's industry; changes in Law or GAAP; epidemics, pandemics and other public health events; acts of war, terrorism and natural disasters; the announcement or pendency of the transactions; and failure to meet projections. The disproportionate-impact modifier applies only to the economic-conditions, industry-conditions and war/terrorism carveouts; it does NOT apply to the change-in-Law or pandemic carveouts in this agreement."}

{"id": 203, "title": "MAUD deal points pack — Silverline Data Systems deal protection and termination note to file (Sections 5.1, 5.3, 7.3 and 8.9)", "doc_type": "memorandum", "related_shape": "maud-deal-points", "body": "NOTE TO FILE — Silverline Data Systems / Aurelian Summit Group: deal protection, interim covenant and termination provisions, conformed from the execution version of the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated July 20, 2026 (Sections 5.1, 5.3, 7.3 and 8.9). Prepared by Ellsworth & Crane LLP for the deal-points survey grid. For the avoidance of doubt in the survey grid: this agreement contains NO go-shop provision of any kind; the non-solicitation covenant applies from execution of the Agreement, and there is no post-signing window during which the Company may solicit competing proposals.

Section 5.1 Interim Operating Covenant. From the date of the Agreement until the earlier of the Effective Time and termination, except with Parent's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), the Company shall use commercially reasonable efforts to conduct its business in the ordinary course of business and to preserve intact its material business relationships. Drafting note: unlike the market-majority formulation, this covenant does NOT include a "consistent with past practice" qualifier.

Section 5.3 No Solicitation; Fiduciary Exception; Matching Rights. From and after the date of the Agreement, the Company shall not, and shall cause its Representatives not to, solicit, initiate or knowingly facilitate any Acquisition Proposal. Prior to the Acceptance Time, in response to a bona fide unsolicited written Acquisition Proposal that the Company Board determines in good faith (after consultation with outside counsel and its financial advisor) constitutes or would reasonably be expected to lead to a Superior Proposal, and where failure to act would be inconsistent with the directors' fiduciary duties under applicable Law, the Company may furnish information under an Acceptable Confidentiality Agreement and engage in discussions. Before any Adverse Recommendation Change or fiduciary termination, the Company must give Parent five (5) Business Days' prior written notice and negotiate in good faith during that period (the "Match Period"); each subsequent material modification to the financial terms of the Superior Proposal triggers a new notice and an additional two (2) Business Days' Match Period.

Section 7.3 Company Termination Fee. Upon (a) a fiduciary termination by the Company to accept a Superior Proposal, (b) termination by Parent following an Adverse Recommendation Change, or (c) a tail-period transaction (an Acquisition Proposal publicly made before termination and consummated, or made the subject of a definitive agreement, within nine (9) months after termination for Outside Date failure or Company breach), the Company shall pay Parent a termination fee of $86,500,000 in cash (the "Company Termination Fee"), payable at most once.

Section 8.9 Remedies. The parties' remedies are asymmetric. Parent and Purchaser are entitled to specific performance of the Company's covenants under Sections 5.1 and 5.3. The Company, however, is NOT entitled to specific performance to compel Parent or Purchaser to commence or consummate the Offer or to effect the Closing; the Company's sole and exclusive remedy against Parent and Purchaser for any failure to consummate the Offer or the Merger is an action for monetary damages, capped at $150,000,000 in the aggregate (the "Parent Liability Cap"). No separate reverse termination fee is provided."}
